changes: Already set up? Updating keeps everything: your folders, channels, settings and projects stay, and the new setup window never opens for you (don't run SETUP.cmd).

New editor: a Filmora-style timeline with a Revise view. Watch your draft, pause and type or say what to change, and it's added at that moment. Double-click a caption to fix a word, or double-click a product review intro's words to retype them (Save, or Save + update intro now: about 4-5 minutes, same shots).

Train your style: Settings -> Train your style. Name it, pick what your videos are closest to, then drop anything: finished videos you like, a raw recording, a project from Premiere, CapCut, Filmora, Kdenlive or Shotcut (or an XML / FCPXML / EDL / OpenTimelineIO export from DaVinci Resolve, Vegas, Final Cut or Avid), a clip with a feature you want, your logo or an opening clip. Or pick videos you already made in the Studio (their notes are learned too), say what it should always do in your own words, or add a text card to open every video (a verse, a quote). The Studio measures camera layout, cuts, pauses, zooms, music and head turns, Claude looks at the frames and writes the style. Your logo / opening / ending go into every build by themselves, and every note you give on a video of that style teaches it more (Settings shows what it learned; remove anything). No Minecraft graphics on a gaming-based style unless your examples have them.
Everything you teach lives in one folder, my_style (your types, their rules, the AI director's taught examples): updates never change it, so you never retrain after an update.
Camera layout detection: 1 camera / 2 on screen / screen + camera / vertical / no face, and head turns on one camera (New Project suggests your own type when one fits).
Updates ask you: when a new version is out, the Studio shows a popup with what's new and an Update now / Later button (Later asks again the next day).

Free beta, anonymous edit stats: finished videos send numbers only (lengths, cut counts, what you undid) to help improve cutting. Never words, files, audio or video. Off switch + Delete my stats in Settings.

One-click setup: double-click SETUP.cmd. It installs Python, FFmpeg, Node, Git and Claude Code for you (no restarting windows), checks everything, adds a Creator Studio Desktop shortcut, then opens the Studio with a setup window: it checks FFmpeg, Node and Claude (a fix button for anything missing, Claude sign-in included), asks where your recordings, projects and music go, the captions default and your channel name, one question per screen. Settings -> Setup runs it again.
Approved edits are now the answer key for their recording: a rebuild can never quietly bring back a take you already cut (approved_cuts).

Draft self-check: every finished draft is transcribed and listened to for repeats and retakes before it's marked ready (draft_audit), and the camera that's really on screen is measured from the picture (shown_cam).
Intros: a new KV pixel-box intro template (assets/Graphics/HyperFrames/_templates/kv-pixelbox) and a bigger intro library.
Descriptions: the description writer follows the Top 5 / Top 10 format for list videos and only uses links already in the project's own files.
Player bar on every video: -10 s / +10 s and 1x / 1.5x / 2x speed that sticks.
Phone review page (Studio/ui/m.html): watch a draft and send notes from your phone while Studio runs on your PC.
Schedule a build: start a draft at a time you pick (project page: Schedule).
Everything builds on your own PC: no second machine, no other AI services. Claude only.
New video types: Haul (one long phone recording, 1080p60, beat per section, captions on intro + outro) and Short (raw vertical recordings: 1080x1920, tight trim, captions, hook headline, punch-ins).
Render queue: one GPU build at a time, a Queue page, live revision statuses, a smoother progress bar with ETA and a stuck warning.

Captions (opt-in, per project): 8 new styles popular on YouTube and Shorts - one big word at a time, karaoke fill, highlighter box, two-tone keywords, soft neon glow, podcast lower captions, minimal caps and typewriter - picked from a grid of previews. All free Google Fonts, sized to fit vertical Shorts too; bottom styles are greyed out on gaming videos.

Set up your music: the Studio (and the setup interview) finds the music already on your PC - Music, Downloads, Desktop, Videos, OneDrive, music folders on other drives - and sorts it into a mood library (chill, upbeat, hype, dark, cinematic, lo-fi) by listening to it. It sorts everything by itself (no list to tick): your files are never moved or deleted (hard links or copies), tracks with vocals or producer tags are left out, and you get a report. Right-click any song in a song picker to change its mood or remove it from the library for good (Settings -> Music puts it back). A track's mood no longer drifts when you add music.
Music picker: chooses from your whole music folder by mood, no repeats across a channel's last 15 videos, vocal-scanned.
Intros: new templates (P21 glowing phone, R21 editor cut), a quality gate (intro_score / intro_check), named-site page scrolls, creator clips, product library, faster fix passes.
Review pipeline: cleaner joins (no mid-sentence starts, breath-tail joins), repeat guard, second-mic gap detection, B-roll per product, self-talk + retake cleanup.
Screen recordings: topic sections + music changes, cursor zooms on what you talk about.
Privacy: new on-screen personal-info scan + blur (pii_scan / pii_blur / pii_check).
Studio redesign (new look) and many speed-ups.

Export to a video editor: in the editor, More -> Export to Premiere / Resolve / Final Cut. You get a timeline of your cut that opens in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Vegas or Final Cut (XML / FCPXML), any editor (EDL) or OpenTimelineIO, linked to your original recording with every cut in place, sections as markers, B-roll on track 2 and the music bed on its own track. CapCut and Filmora can't import a timeline, so it points you to Resolve (free) instead.
